To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical state of a granular system is the state at which the Mohr-Cou-lomb envelope and the critical compaction envelope intersect.

the rupture strength of an interlocked over-compacted granulate is the sum of the Mohr-Columb shear strength plus the interlocking strength, and that critical state for an interlocked overcompacted granular material corresponds to the intersection of the critical compaction envelope with the Mohr–Coulomb envelope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rupture strength of granular materials and the critical states they exhibit.
the rupture strength of granular materials.
the rupture strength of over-compacted granules and the physics-chemistry of granules at critical state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mohr-Columb strength envelope is the most fundamental strength envelope of all.
cohesion is a real material property and is not an empirical fitting parameter.
the Mohr-Coumb theory of strength is valid for granular materials, but the contribution of cohesion is negligible for over-compacted granules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mohr-Cou-lomb theory of strength is a useful tool for the analysis of granular material strength, but that the interlocking strength is an important additional factor in over-compacted materials.
the Mohr-Coumb theory of strength for a granular system is not complete.
interlocking is the key to understanding the rupture behavior of over-compacted granules, and that critical state provides the framework for understanding the rupture strength of granular materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cohesion is not a material constant but is a function of the degree of over-compaction of a granular assembly.
interlocking is a fundamental property of granular materials, and that the rupture strength of over-compacted granules can be described as the sum of three contributions.
cohesion is a manifestation of over-compaction and not a fundamental property of a granular assembly.
